Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:110888
Court No. - 70
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 19550 of 2024

Applicant :- Ajeet Singh
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Harishchandra Dubey,Ram Mohan
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Heard Sri Harishchandra Dubey, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Rajeev Dhar Dubey,
learned Aga, for the State.

2.  The instant bail application has been moved on behalf of the applicant with the prayer to release him on bail in Case Crime No.81 of 2023, under Sections 498A and 304B IPC and Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Dannahar, District Mainpuri during pendency of the trial.

3. FIR of the present case was lodged against the applicant and his family members and according to the FIR, marriage of the applicant was solemnized with the deceased on 30.6.2021 and after marriage applicant and his family members tortured her for demand of dowry and on 11.4.2023 applicant and his family members committed the murder of the deceased for want of dowry.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is the husband of the deceased and on the basis of false allegation he has been made accused in the present matter.

sentences.text: He further submits that actually deceased was obstinate natured lady and she also remained under depression due to the reason that however more then two years have been passed since marriage but she could not conceive and only due to these reasons she committed suicide by hanging herself.
6. He further submits that post mortem report of the deceased also suggests that deceased died due to hanging.

7. He further submits that there is no specific allegation of dowry in the FIR, however, when the statement of the informant was recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. then informant started making allegation that there was a demand of motorcycle and a golden chain and this fact clearly suggests that on the basis of false allegation of demand of dowry applicant and his family members have been made accused in the present matter.

8. He further submits that however when informant appeared before the trial court as PW-1 then initially he supported the prosecution case but subsequently he did not support the prosecution case and on the application moved by the prosecution he has been declared hostile.
9. He further submits that when mother of the deceased was examined by trial court as PW-2 then since beginning she did not support the prosecution case and she has also been declared hostile.
10. He further submits that applicant is not having any previous criminal history and he is in jail in the present matter since 12.6.2023, i.e., for more than a year.

11. Per contra, learned AGA, however, opposed the prayerfor bail and submits that applicant is the husband of the deceased and his wife died within two years of her marriage under abnormal circumstances in her matrimonial home but he could not dispute the fact that deceased died due to hanging and there was no specific demand of dowry in the FIR and parents of the deceased during trial have been declared hostile and applicant is in jail for more than a year.
12.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

13. However, applicant is the husband of the deceased but it appears that his wife died under abnormal circumstances within seven years of her marriage in her matrimonial home but it reflects that there was no specific allegation of demand of dowry in the FIR
, however, informant in his statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. disclosed that deceased was tortured by applicant and his family members due to demand of a motorcycle and a golden chain.

14. Further, autopsy report of the deceased suggests that deceased died due to hanging and,
therefore, argument advanced by learned counsel for the applicant cannot be completely brushed aside at this stage.
15. Further, record also suggests that during trial when parents of the deceased appeared before the trial court as PW-1 and 2 then they have been declared hostile.

Ajeet Singh vs State Of U.P. on 9 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142757675/
2 16.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, applicant is not having any previous criminal history and in the present matter he is in jail since 12.6.2023.

17.Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
18. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

19. Let the applicant-Ajeet Singh be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
20. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.
